source_title: Restaurant Brands International Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results
source_excerpt:
Consolidated System-wide Sales grow 6.2% year-over-year, including 9.0% in International Global Comparable Sales of 3.8%, including 8.4% at BK US and 3.9% at International RBI returns $1.3 billion of capital to shareholders year to date through dividends and share repurchases RBI remains on track for 8% organic Adjusted Operating Income growth in 2026
MIAMI , Oct. 29, 2026 /CNW/ -- Restaurant Brands International Inc. ("RBI") (NYSE: QSR ) (TSX: QSR) (TSX: QSP) today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Josh Kobza, Chief Executive Officer of RBI commented, "At our Investor Day earlier this year, we highlighted what makes RBI a strong business â four iconic global brands, the ability to invest for long-term growth, and talented teams and franchisees around the world. Those strengths are on display again this quarter, with over 3% global comparable sales led by outperformance at Burger King and steady growth at International and Tim Hortons. I'm proud of what we're accomplishing together. Across our brands, we're continuing to listen to our guests and act on their feedback to deliver the quality, service, and convenience they expect every day."

Reporting Segments We have six operating and reportable segments, including four franchisor segments for our Tim Hortons, Burger King, Popeyes, and Firehouse Subs brands in the U.S. and Canada ("TH", "BK", "PLK", and "FHS", respectively) and a fifth franchisor segment for all of our brands in the rest of the world ("INTL"). Additionally, we have a sixth operating and reportable segment, Restaurant Holdings ("RH"), which includes the operations of (i) Burger King restaurants acquired in our acquisition of Carrols Restaurant Group Inc. (the "Carrols Acquisition"), (ii) restaurants acquired in our acquisition of Popeyes China ("PLK China") ("PLK China Acquisition"), and (iii) Firehouse Subs Brazil ("FHS Brazil") restaurants.
RBI maintains the franchisor dynamics in its TH, BK, PLK, FHS, and INTL segments ("Five Franchisor Segments") to report results consistent with how the business will be managed long-term. This approach reflects RBI's intent to refranchise the vast majority of the Carrols Burger King restaurants and to find new investors for PLK China and FHS Brazil and sunset the RH segment. RH results include Company restaurant sales and expenses, including expenses associated with royalties, rent, and advertising. These expenses are recognized, as applicable, as revenues in the respective franchisor segments (BK for the Carrols Burger King restaurants and INTL for PLK China and FHS Brazil restaurants) and eliminated upon consolidation.
Items Affecting Comparability Burger King China On February 14, 2025, we acquired substantially all of the remaining equity interests in Burger King China ("BK China"). For 2025, BK China was classified as held for sale and reported as discontinued operations. As such, for 2025, results for BK China were not recognized in the INTL segment. However, BK China KPIs continued to be included in our INTL segment KPIs.
On January 30, 2026, we established a joint venture with CPE Alder Investment Limited, a fund managed by CPE ("CPE"), with respect to the operations of BK China (such joint venture, the "BK China JV"). CPE invested $350 million of primary capital into the BK China JV. Following the transaction, we deconsolidated BK China and began accounting for our remaining 17% equity interest in the BK China JV under the equity method of accounting and recognizing franchise revenue, primarily related to royalties, in our INTL segment. We refer to the acquisition of BK China and the subsequent establishment of the BK China JV collectively as the "BK China Transactions."
2026 Convention Timing Impact on Franchise and Property Results In 2025, PLK and BK INTL hosted conventions in Q2, BK and FHS hosted conventions in Q3, and TH did not host a convention. In 2026, PLK and FHS hosted conventions in Q3, TH and BK will host conventions in Q4, and BK INTL will not host a convention. Convention-related revenues and expenses are recognized in each segment's Franchise and property revenues and Segment F&P expenses, respectively, and have an immaterial net AOI impact.

For the third quarter, the increase in Total revenues was driven by higher Supply chain sales primarily due to increases in equipment sales to franchisees and commodity prices. The increase in Total revenues was also driven by increased System-wide Sales. Results also reflect an unfavorable FX Impact of $16 million. Excluding the FX Impact, Total revenues increased by $27 million.
The increase in Adjusted Operating Income was primarily driven by tariff refunds and increased System-wide Sales. Results also reflect an unfavorable FX Impact of $4 million. Excluding the FX Impact, Adjusted Operating Income increased by $17 million.

Franchise and property revenues include intersegment revenues with RH consisting of royalties and rent of $29 million and $86 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, and $28 million and $83 million during three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, which are eliminated in consolidation.
Advertising revenues and other services include intersegment revenues with RH consisting of advertising contributions and tech fees of $22 million and $67 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, and $21 million and $63 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, which are eliminated in consolidation.
As a reminder, BK segment results are presented consistently with our franchisor model. As such, results include intersegment Franchise and property revenues and Advertising revenues and other services from the Carrols Burger King restaurants included in RH (as footnoted above).
Burger King US Reclaim the Flame Burger King is executing its multi-year "Reclaim the Flame" plan to accelerate sales growth and drive franchisee profitability. This plan includes investing up to $700 million through year-end 2028, comprised of advertising and digital investments (which were completed in 2024) and high-quality remodels and relocations, restaurant technology, kitchen equipment, and building enhancements ("Royal Reset"). As of September 30, 2026, we have funded $198 million out of up to $550 million planned toward the Royal Reset investments.
Third Quarter 2026 Results The increase in Total revenues was primarily driven by the increase in Comparable Sales, partially offset by the net impact of refranchisings.
The increase in Adjusted Operating Income was primarily driven by the increase in Comparable Sales.
For the third quarter, the increase in Total revenues was primarily driven by higher Company restaurant sales due to restaurants acquired during the period, partially offset by lower Advertising revenues and other services due primarily to a decline in advertising fund contributions.
The decrease in Adjusted Operating Income was primarily driven by a decline in Comparable Sales and an increase in Segment G&A, primarily driven by higher compensation-related expenses, partially offset by higher Company restaurant sales.
For the third quarter, the increases in Total revenues and Adjusted Operating Income were primarily driven by the increase in restaurant count.

For the third quarter, the increase in Total revenues was primarily driven by higher royalty revenues from Burger King and Popeyes restaurants resulting from increased System-wide Sales, as well as the resumption of royalty revenues from BK China. Results also reflect an unfavorable FX Impact of $2 million. Excluding the FX Impact, Total revenues increased by $23 million.
The increase in Adjusted Operating Income was driven by revenue growth, partially offset by an increase in Segment G&A primarily due to higher compensation-related expenses. Restaurant occupancy and other expenses include intersegment royalties and property expenses of $30 million and $88 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, and $28 million and $83 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, which are eliminated in consolidation.
Advertising expenses and other services include intersegment advertising expenses and tech fees of $22 million and $67 million during the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, and $21 million and $63 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, which are eliminated in consolidation.
The RH segment includes results from (i) Burger King restaurants acquired as part of the Carrols Acquisition and (ii) PLK China and FHS Brazil restaurants. RH segment results reflect the impact of refranchising Carrols Burger King restaurants as well as incremental investments in the PLK China and FHS Brazil start-up businesses.
For the third quarter, the increase in Total revenues was primarily driven by an increase in BK US Comparable Sales and an increase in PLK China restaurant count, partially offset by the refranchisings of Carrols Burger King restaurants.
The decrease in Adjusted Operating Income was primarily driven by an increase in Company restaurant expenses and Segment G&A, partially offset by higher revenues. The increase in Company restaurant expenses reflects higher Carrols Burger King Company restaurant expenses, primarily driven by increased sales, as well as expenses related to scaling our international start-up businesses. The increase in Segment G&A was primarily due to higher compensation-related expenses.
Cash and Liquidity The RBI Board of Directors has declared a dividend of $0.65 per common share and partnership exchangeable unit of RBI LP for the fourth quarter of 2026. The dividend will be payable on January 5, 2027 to shareholders and unitholders of record at the close of business on December 22, 2026.
On August 6, 2025, our Board of Directors approved a share repurchase program authorizing the repurchase of up to $1,000 million of our common shares from September 15, 2025 through September 30, 2027. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, we repurchased 817,041 of our common shares for $61 million and 2,784,549 of Class B exchangeable limited partnership units for $214 million, excluding excise taxes. Of these repurchases, 28,010 common shares had not yet settled as of September 30, 2026 and therefore were not retired at that date. As of September 30, 2026, we had $768 million remaining under the share repurchase authorization.
Subsequent Events Subsequent to September 30, 2026 through October 23, 2026, we repurchased 235,276 of our common shares for $17 million and as of October 23, 2026 had $751 million remaining under the share repurchase authorization.
2026 Financial Guidance For 2026, RBI continues to expect:
Segment G&A (excluding RH) for 2026 between $600 million and $620 million;
RH AOI of approximately $10 to $20 million;
Adjusted Interest Expense, net between $500 million and $520 million; and
Consolidated capital expenditures, tenant inducements and incentives (including RH), or "Total Capex and Cash Inducements" of around $400 million.
Long-Term Algorithm RBI continues to expect the following long-term consolidated performance on average, from 2024 to 2028:
8%+ organic Adjusted Operating Income growth.
In addition, RBI continues to expect to reach 5%+ Net Restaurant Growth towards the end of its algorithm period.

About Restaurant Brands International Inc. Restaurant Brands International Inc. is one of the world's largest quick service restaurant companies with over $49 billion in annual system-wide sales and over 33,000 restaurants in more than 120 countries and territories. RBI owns four of the world's most prominent and iconic quick service restaurant brands â TIM HORTONSÂ®, BURGER KINGÂ®, POPEYESÂ®, and FIREHOUSE SUBSÂ®. These independently operated brands have been serving their respective guests, franchisees and communities for decades. Through its Restaurant Brands for Good framework, RBI is improving sustainable outcomes related to its food, the planet, and people and communities.
RBI's principal executive offices are in Miami, Florida. In North America, RBI's brands are headquartered in their home markets where they were founded decades ago: Canada for Tim Hortons and the U.S. for Burger King, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs. To learn more about RBI, please visit the company's website at www.rbi.com .
